Stage 01

Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO transparency, Apostille authentication chain, official name clearance restricted wordlist, and pre-incorporation statutory fee budget.

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Key instruments include Law 10/2010 of 28 April on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing; Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May implementing Law 10/2010; Law 10/2014 of 26 June on the regulation, supervision and solvency of credit institutions, as relevant to regulated financial counterparties; Royal Decree 609/2023 of 11 July establishing the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership (RCTIR); and the Spanish Companies Act, consolidated by Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July. Companies must identify and maintain adequate records of their beneficial owners. Generally, a natural person holding or controlling, directly or indirectly, more than 25% of capital or voting rights, or otherwise exercising control, is a beneficial owner. RCTIR access is subject to statutory access rules and applicable data-protection and EU-law requirements.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

A Spanish registered office is mandatory for an S.L. A virtual-office address may be acceptable for registry and correspondence purposes if it is a genuine address permitted by law and the company can receive official notices there. It does not by itself establish adequate operational substance. For a clinical-trial CRO, maintain demonstrable management, personnel, records, data-protection controls, secure trial documentation, and inspection access appropriate to the actual functions performed. A CRO does not generally require a standalone Spanish CRO operating licence solely by virtue of that label; clinical-trial authorization, sponsor obligations, ethics review, and site requirements apply to the relevant trial and role under Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 and Spanish Law 14/2007 and implementing rules. Confirm the precise role and activity with AEMPS and the competent ethics committee.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Central Mercantile Registry for company-name certification and the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for incorporation registration.

Governing statute

Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), principally Articles 4, 19-32, 58-63, 78-80, 210-241, and 249-250; Law 14/2013 and Law 18/2022 apply to electronic incorporation and reduced-capital Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada rules.

Formation / constitutional filings

Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución) filed for registration with the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry, supported by a valid company-name certificate from the Central Mercantile Registry.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 58 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

The statutory minimum capital of an Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. Until equity reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve and, upon liquidation with insufficient assets, shareholders may have supplementary liability up to the difference between EUR 3,000 and the subscribed capital. A bank escrow account is not mandatory where the founders state in the deed that they are jointly and severally liable for the accuracy of the cash contribution; if used, the bank certificate must identify the deposited amount and account.

Funding & unlock path: Obtain municipal opening, activity, or premises approval where required and comply with the applicable regional fire-safety rules, the Spanish Building Code, and workplace risk-prevention legislation. Maintain fire detection and extinguishing systems, emergency plans, evacuation routes, electrical and structural-load certifications, and periodic inspections. Laboratory, biological, chemical, cold-storage, or investigational-product premises require additional biosafety, occupational-health, temperature-control, and hazardous-material controls.

Paid-in capital rule: The statutory minimum capital of an Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. Until equity reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve and, upon liquidation with insufficient assets, shareholders may have supplementary liability up to the difference between EUR 3,000 and the subscribed capital. A bank escrow account is not mandatory where the founders state in the deed that they are jointly and severally liable for the accuracy of the cash contribution; if used, the bank certificate must identify the deposited amount and account.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
RESOLVED, that the Company accept and ratify the subscription and full payment of its issued share capital by the founding shareholder in accordance with the incorporation deed and articles of association. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at the address stated in the deed and recorded with the Mercantile Registry. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed sole director, or, if applicable, that the persons named in the deed be appointed as directors, each accepting office and declaring eligibility. RESOLVED, that the appointed officer(s) be authorized to obtain tax, banking, electronic-certification, employment, and regulatory registrations required for commencement of business.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Mandatory Environmental Clearance

Spanish Agency of Medicines and Medical Devices (Agencia Española de Medicamentos y Productos Sanitarios, AEMPS), together with the competent autonomous-community health authority and accredited research ethics committee for clinical-trial activities. Spain has no general standalone manufacturing licence for an office-based CRO; licensing is activity-specific.

Category: Clinical-trial authorization (autorización de ensayo clínico) and the applicable AEMPS notification or registration for the entity's defined role, including sponsor or CRO functions. Separate authorization or certification may apply to investigational-medicinal-product manufacture, import, storage, distribution, or biological sample handling.

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and official portal at https://www.agenciatributaria.es/

E-government filing portal

Foreign entities obtain NIF by submitting Form 036 or online registration via AEAT portal, including proof of incorporation, fiscal domicile, and tax representative appointment; Spanish SL entities receive NIF automatically upon incorporation with Registro Mercantil.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — Foreign entities obtain NIF by submitting Form 036 or online registration via AEAT portal, including proof of incorporation, fiscal domicile, and tax representative appointment; Spanish SL entities receive NIF automatically upon incorporation with Registro Mercantil.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation

Available election forms

No check-the-box elections available; hybrid mismatch rules under EU ATAD directives apply, with limited small-business regimes for qualifying entities below turnover thresholds.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

30,000 EUR annual turnover

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

0% VAT rate for goods exported outside the EU or services to non-EU clients performed outside Spain and not involving immovable property; proof required that transaction is exported or service performed abroad.

  • Customs Export Declaration
  • Bill of Lading
  • Inward Remittance Certificate

Mandatory facturación electrónica for B2B transactions since 2023; real-time fiscal clearance via AEAT integrated systems, API submissions required for large taxpayers, and digital invoice stamping.

AEAT audits may result in fines up to 100% of evaded tax, interest, and surcharges; fraudulent claims trigger criminal penalties and permanent revocation of zero-rating rights.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain, as a full EU member state, operates under complete capital account and current account convertibility. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are permitted without prior approval, subject only to standard tax reporting and beneficial ownership verification.

Export proceeds surrender rules

No mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds applies to service-based transactions under EU free movement of capital and payments rules. Voluntary surrender for statistical purposes may be requested but is not obligatory.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Limited feasibility for offshore digital EMIs; Spanish law requires local banking or EMI licensing with full AML/KYC compliance, rendering pure remote fintech structures non-viable without local incorporation.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Unexplained large or frequent inbound transfers lacking commercial rationale

Root cause: Unexplained large or frequent inbound transfers lacking commercial rationale

Defense evidence: Multinational sponsor contracts, clinical trial protocols, milestone payment schedules, board resolutions authorizing CRO services, and source-of-funds statements
Beneficial ownership opacity or shell-company indicators

Root cause: Beneficial ownership opacity or shell-company indicators

Defense evidence: Notarized shareholder agreements, ownership chain documentation, and corporate structure chart

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Compliant inbound capital via SWIFT MT103 using purpose code 'Capital Contribution' or 'Equity Injection'; require board resolution, foreign exchange declaration, and proof of equity origin.Clearing through SWIFT MT103 for milestone and service payments; Commercial Letters of Credit for trade-related disbursements; all transactions routed via correspondent banks with purpose codes such as 'Service Fees', 'Trial Expenses', or 'CRO Management Fees'.Forward contractsNon-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs)Currency swaps

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Limited feasibility for offshore digital EMIs; Spanish law requires local banking or EMI licensing with full AML/KYC compliance, rendering pure remote fintech structures non-viable without local incorporation.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25% general corporate income tax rate. Newly incorporated entities may generally apply a 15% rate in the first tax period in which they obtain a positive taxable base and the immediately following tax period, subject to statutory exclusions and conditions.

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% Spanish withholding tax generally applies to dividends and other profit distributions paid by a Spanish resident company to a non-resident shareholder, subject to domestic exemptions, tax treaties, and procedural requirements.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Modelo 200 is filed within 25 calendar days following the six months after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer ending on 31 December, the normal filing period is 1 to 25 July of the following year. Modelo 202 advance payments are generally due during the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December; electronic filing is generally available through the 15th calendar day, with payment completed through the applicable banking procedure. The relevant filing calendar must be verified annually, including weekend and public-holiday adjustments.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Generally due during the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December. Electronic filing deadlines and payment arrangements may close earlier than the statutory submission window.

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Identification and tax-period fields Enter the Spanish tax identification number (NIF), legal name, entity type, tax period start and end dates, registered address, and applicable tax administration details. A non-resident shareholder does not file the SL's Modelo 200 merely because it owns shares. The Spanish SL files using its own Spanish NIF. Non-resident directors and shareholders must be correctly identified where requested. Late or missing Modelo 200 filing may generate fixed penalties where there is no tax debt and percentage-based penalties where tax is payable or refundable, generally under General Tax Law provisions, with reductions potentially available for prompt payment or conformity. Incorrect returns may incur penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the improperly unpaid amount, depending on concealment, fraud, and aggravating circumstances. Transfer-pricing documentation failures may generate separate fixed or percentage-based penalties.
Taxable base and tax liability Calculate the adjusted taxable base, apply the applicable tax rate, and determine gross corporate income tax liability. Use the Spanish corporate tax rate applicable to the taxpayer and period. Do not apply treaty withholding rates to the SL's own corporate tax computation. Transfer-pricing documentation failures may generate separate fixed or percentage-based penalties.
Withholdings, payments on account, and advance payments Credit Spanish corporate tax advance payments, recoverable withholdings, and other permitted prepayments against the final liability. Foreign withholding tax generally requires a foreign tax credit analysis and evidence of payment. Spanish withholding suffered by the SL must be supported by certificates or AEAT records. Transfer-pricing documentation failures may generate separate fixed or percentage-based penalties.
Balance payable or refundable State the final amount payable to AEAT or the refund requested, including the selected payment or refund bank-account details. The bank account and refund documentation must be controlled by the Spanish taxpayer and supported by accounting records. A refund request may trigger verification of substance, withholding certificates, and related-party transactions. Late or missing Modelo 200 filing may generate fixed penalties where there is no tax debt and percentage-based penalties where tax is payable or refundable, generally under General Tax Law provisions, with reductions potentially available for prompt payment or conformity. Annual accounts and electronic signature Submit the return electronically with the authorized electronic certificate and retain the return, accounting records, tax reconciliation, transfer-pricing documentation, and supporting schedules. A non-resident parent may authorize a Spanish representative or director to file, but the Spanish SL remains responsible for the accuracy and completeness of the return. Modelo 202 advance-payment calculation Calculate advance payments using the prior-year tax-liability method or the current-period taxable-base method where mandatory or elected, depending on the taxpayer's turnover and statutory conditions. A foreign-owned SL is not exempt from advance payments. Large-company rules and the current-period method may apply based on turnover thresholds and the taxpayer's status. Late filing and late payment may trigger fixed or percentage-based tax penalties, late-payment surcharges, and interest. Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Spain does not use a single universal monetary threshold for all transfer-pricing documentation. The general materiality threshold commonly relevant to the documentation exemption is EUR 250,000 in aggregate controlled transactions with the same related person or entity during the tax period, subject to exclusions and special rules, including transactions involving real estate and certain intangible assets. Local File and Master File obligations must also be assessed under the taxpayer's consolidated-group status, turnover, transaction type, and Spanish transfer-pricing regulations. Taxpayers with net turnover below EUR 45 million may generally use simplified documentation where permitted, but the EUR 250,000 threshold is not a blanket exemption from the arm's-length principle or record-keeping duties.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not operate a standalone UAE-style Economic Substance Regulation for ordinary Spanish companies. Substance is nevertheless material under the arm's-length principle, beneficial-ownership rules, EU anti-abuse rules, the principal-purpose test, controlled foreign company rules, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule, anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation rules, and Spanish tax-residence and effective-management analysis. The SL should maintain Spanish personnel or outsourced operational capacity appropriate to its CRO functions, decision-making evidence, premises or controlled work infrastructure, clinical-trial systems, regulatory compliance, risk management, contracts, and contemporaneous records. A low-substance entity receiving group charges or remitting royalties, interest, or dividends may face denial of deductions, treaty benefits, recharacterization, withholding assessments, and penalties.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax evasion and fraudulent corporate income tax reporting

Statutory sanction: Administrative penalties may generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax depending on concealment and aggravating factors. Where the tax quota defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000 for a tax period, the conduct may constitute a criminal tax offence, generally punishable by imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of 1 to 6 times the amount defrauded. Aggravated cases, including amounts exceeding EUR 600,000 or organized fraud, may carry imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and a fine of 2 to 6 times the amount defrauded.

Director personal liability: Directors and de facto managers may incur criminal liability, civil liability arising from the offence, and subsidiary or joint-and-several tax liability under Spanish General Tax Law where statutory conditions are met. Courts may impose precautionary asset measures and, in criminal proceedings, restrictions affecting travel or passports where legally justified; a travel ban is not an automatic tax consequence.
Transfer-pricing manipulation and unsupported related-party deductions

Statutory sanction: AEAT may make an arm's-length primary adjustment, impose secondary tax consequences, deny deductions, assess withholding tax, and apply transfer-pricing documentation penalties. Documentation and data failures may attract fixed penalties per omitted or inaccurate item and, in material cases, percentage-based penalties linked to the adjustment or transaction amounts under the General Tax Law.

Director personal liability: Directors may be jointly or subsidiarily liable where they deliberately authorize abusive accounting or tax conduct, fail to prevent a statutory breach, or cause non-payment after assessment. Criminal liability may arise if the conduct forms part of tax fraud, false accounting, or document offences.
False R&D or technological-innovation tax-credit claim

Statutory sanction: The credit may be denied or recaptured with late-payment interest and tax penalties. False invoices, fabricated technical reports, or deliberate concealment may escalate to accounting, document, or tax-criminal offences.

Director personal liability: Directors approving unsupported claims may face tax-liability extension, civil restitution, professional consequences, and criminal liability if intentional falsification or fraud is established.
Improper treaty relief and withholding-tax failure

Statutory sanction: The Spanish payer may be assessed for underwithheld tax, late-payment interest, and withholding penalties. Failure to file or incorrect filing of Modelo 216 or Modelo 296 may generate additional formal penalties.

Director personal liability: Directors and legal representatives may become personally liable for unpaid withholding tax where statutory conditions for liability extension are satisfied, particularly where the payment structure was knowingly designed to defeat Spanish withholding.
Shell company, artificial residence, or beneficial-ownership abuse

Statutory sanction: AEAT may deny treaty or EU directive benefits, recharacterize income, apply controlled foreign company or anti-abuse provisions, disallow deductions, assess withholding, and impose penalties. Transactions may be challenged under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule or principal-purpose test.

Director personal liability: Directors may face joint-and-several or subsidiary tax liability, civil claims, and criminal liability where sham arrangements, fraud, false accounting, or concealment are proven. Corporate limited liability does not protect directors from their own unlawful conduct.
Clinical-trial regulatory and tax-record integrity failure

Statutory sanction: Regulatory sanctions may include orders to correct, suspension or withdrawal of authorization, administrative fines, and contractual damages. Tax consequences may include denial of deductions, VAT and corporate tax assessments, withholding issues, and penalties. Serious falsification or patient-safety misconduct may constitute a criminal offence.

Director personal liability: Directors and responsible officers may face administrative, civil, and criminal exposure for deliberate or negligent breaches, including restitution, disqualification, and imprisonment where the underlying conduct satisfies criminal-law elements.
Anti-money-laundering and sanctions compliance

Statutory sanction: Under Spanish AML legislation, serious and very serious infringements may attract substantial monetary penalties, public reprimand or publication, temporary or permanent disqualification from management functions, and other measures. Sanctions depend on the classification, severity, benefit, recurrence, and responsible-person status. Sanctions breaches may also trigger EU or Spanish restrictive-measures enforcement and criminal liability.

Director personal liability: Directors, compliance officers, and de facto managers may be personally sanctioned or prosecuted where they consented to, tolerated, or negligently failed to prevent the breach. Asset freezes, precautionary measures, and court-ordered travel restrictions may arise in criminal or sanctions proceedings but are not automatic for every AML breach.
Accounting, invoice, and corporate-book falsification

Statutory sanction: Tax adjustments, penalties, rejection of accounts, shareholder claims, director disqualification, and criminal sanctions for falsifying commercial documents, accounting records, or tax declarations may apply.

Director personal liability: Directors may be personally liable for losses caused to the company, shareholders, creditors, AEAT, or third parties. Criminal sanctions may include imprisonment and fines where the statutory elements of document, accounting, insolvency, or tax offences are met.
Late filing, non-payment, and insolvency misconduct

Statutory sanction: Fixed and percentage-based tax penalties, late-payment surcharges, interest, collection proceedings, account or asset attachments, and potential insolvency-law consequences may apply. Deliberate asset dissipation or creditor preference may create additional civil or criminal exposure.

Director personal liability: Directors may be liable for tax debts where they cause or permit non-payment, fail to take legally required action during insolvency, or engage in asset dissipation. Civil restitution, management disqualification, and imprisonment may apply in proven criminal or culpable insolvency cases; ordinary late filing does not automatically pierce the corporate veil.
